predecessors.name: Stem Duchy of Swabia
predecessors.text: the Wirtemberg hill at Untertürkheim and the lands round it, in the Duchy of Swabia (county infobox: 'Preceded by Duchy of Swabia')

successors.name: Electorate of Württemberg
successors.text: Cliopatria's Electorate of Württemberg row (1803..1805, 10,032 km2 at most): 'In 1803, Napoleon raised the duchy to be the Electorate of Württemberg'

ledger.x: 1081: Konrad I of Württemberg is first recorded; the Wirtemberg castle gives the county its name.
1250: the Hohenstaufen reign over the Duchy of Swabia ends and 'let the Württembergs expand into the duchy'.
1442: the Treaty of Nürtingen divides the county.
1444: Montbéliard passes to the Urach line.
21 July 1495: the county becomes a duchy.
6 February 1520: the Swabian League sells the duchy to Charles V.
September 1634: the Imperial army takes Württemberg.
1648: the Imperial occupation of Württemberg ends with the Peace of Westphalia.
November 1793: the French Republic occupies Montbéliard.
February 1803: the duchy becomes an electorate.

wars.name: Swabian League expulsion of Ulrich
wars.outcome: Ulrich is expelled; the duchy passes to the Habsburgs (Charles V 1520, Ferdinand 1522).

wars.name: Ulrich's reconquest of Württemberg
wars.outcome: Habsburg defeat at Lauffen; the Treaty of Kaaden (June 1534) recognises Ulrich as duke under Austrian suzerainty.

wars.name: Battle of Nördlingen and the Imperial reoccupation
wars.outcome: The Protestant defeat at Nördlingen lets the Imperial army retake most of Württemberg; the Peace of Prague (May 1635) dissolves the Heilbronn League.

wars.name: War of the Spanish Succession (Villars's invasion)
wars.outcome: A French invasion under Villars in 1707; the Duchy page records no territorial change.

certainty.note: The pages give no boundary lines; the duchy was a patchwork of enclaves and Habsburg, Baden and imperial-city neighbours.
